title: Wasserstein Stability, Couplings Across Volumes, and the $1+1/d$ Moment Thresholds in the Edwards--Anderson Model
authors: Mauris Chueng, Hexiang Wang, Keheng Zhu
abstract: We study the quenched pressure of the nearest-neighbor Edwards--Anderson Ising model with free and periodic boundary conditions. First, we prove that the infinite-volume pressure is $βd$-Lipschitz in the coupling law for the $1$-Wasserstein distance, yielding quantitative thermodynamic limits for spatially inhomogeneous disorder. Second, for periodic volumes, we prove that almost-sure convergence under every joint coupling of the finite-volume disorder arrays is equivalent to complete convergence of the one-volume pressure laws. Third, we prove that $\mathbb{E}\vert{}J\vert{}^{1+1/d}<\infty$ guarantees this universal-coupling conclusion. We further show that this exponent is optimal among uniform power-moment assumptions: for every $1\leq q<1+1/d$, there is a centered symmetric law with finite $q$-th moment for which canonical nested volumes converge almost surely, whereas independently resampled volumes with the same fixed-volume marginals converge in probability but not almost surely. Finally, in dimension one, we prove that the first-moment condition is also necessary for a finite limiting pressure.
summary: This work provides a deep mathematical analysis of the Edwards-Anderson Ising model under random disorder, focusing on the convergence of its thermodynamic pressure. The authors prove that the stability of this limit depends critically on the disorder couplings having a finite moment of order $1+1/d$. This establishes a sharp, universal criterion for the existence of the thermodynamic limit across different coupling constructions.
main_problem: The paper investigates the stability and convergence properties of the quenched pressure in the Edwards-Anderson Ising model under random disorder.
main_result: It establishes that the infinite-volume pressure exhibits Wasserstein stability and that almost-sure convergence requires the disorder couplings to satisfy the moment condition $\mathbb{E}|J|^{1+1/d} < \infty$.
method: The analysis employs tools from probability theory, including Wasserstein distance, strong laws, and Borel-Cantelli lemmas, to compare thermodynamic limits under different coupling assumptions.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing the behavior under joint coupling versus independent resampling of disorder volumes, and the sharpness proof requires constructing specific counterexamples for sub-critical moments.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing quantitative stability bounds using the 1-Wasserstein distance. It then proves the equivalence between almost-sure convergence under all joint couplings and the convergence of one-volume laws. Finally, it rigorously determines the optimal moment threshold, $1+1/d$, for this universal convergence.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework developed for determining the precise moment conditions required for thermodynamic limits in disordered systems is highly relevant to understanding phase transitions and critical behavior in complex quantum materials.
